arxiv-2201-10269.title: Probability estimation and structured output prediction for learning preferences in last mile delivery
arxiv-2201-10269.creator: Rocsildes Canoy, Victor Bucarey, Yves Molenbruch, Maxime Mulamba, Jayanta Mandi, Tias Guns
arxiv-2201-10269.description: Abstract We study the problem of learning the preferences of drivers and planners in the context of last mile delivery. Given a data set containing historical decisions and delivery locations, the goal is to capture the implicit preferences of the decision-makers.

arxiv-2212-04112.title: Fabrication method of a low-loss plasmonic waveguide containing both “plasmonic- friendly” and “plasmonic- unfriendly” metals Journal: ol
arxiv-2212-04112.creator: Vadym Zayets, Iryna Serdeha, Valerii Grygoruk
arxiv-2212-04112.description: Abstract Fabrication technology, which allows a substantial decrease of the plasmonic propagation loss for both “plasmon- friendly” metals like Au, Cu or Al and “plasmon- unfriendly” metals like Co, Fe or Cr, has been developed and experimentally demonstrated. Optimization of the optical confinement is used to reduce the propagation loss below 1 dB per plasmonic device.

arxiv-2212-13170.title: Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation of Ships Using Thermal Imagery
arxiv-2212-13170.creator: Rushil Joshi 1 2 , Ethan Adams 1 3 , Matthew Ziemann 4 2 and Christopher A. Metzler 2
arxiv-2212-13170.description: Abstract The United States coastline spans 95,471 miles [ 1 ] ; a distance that cannot be effectively patrolled or secured by manual human effort alone. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) equipped with infrared cameras and deep-learning based algorithms represent a more efficient alternative for identifying and segmenting objects of interest—namely, ships.

arxiv-2312-12730.title: A Closer Look at the Few-Shot Adaptation of Large Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2312-12730.creator: Julio Silva-RodríguezSina HajimiriIsmail Ben AyedJose DolzÉTS Montreal🖂 julio-jose.silva-rodriguez@etsmtl.ca
arxiv-2312-12730.description: Abstract Efficient transfer learning (ETL) is receiving increasing attention to adapt large pre-trained language-vision models on downstream tasks with a few labeled samples. While significant progress has been made, we reveal that state-of-the-art ETL approaches exhibit strong performance only in narrowly-defined experimental setups, and with a careful adjustment of hyperparameters based on a large corpus of labeled samples.

arxiv-2410-21139.title: uOttawa at LegalLens-2024: Transformer-based Classification Experiments
arxiv-2410-21139.creator: Nima Meghdadi, Diana Inkpen
arxiv-2410-21139.description: Abstract This paper presents the methods used for LegalLens-2024 shared task, which focused on detecting legal violations within unstructured textual data and associating these violations with potentially affected individuals. The shared task included two subtasks: A) Legal Named Entity Recognition (L-NER) and B) Legal Natural Language Inference (L-NLI).

arxiv-2502-18346.title: Testing Thresholds and Spectral Properties of High-Dimensional Random Toroidal Graphs via Edgeworth-Style Expansions.
arxiv-2502-18346.creator: Samuel Baguley, Andreas Göbel, Marcus Pappik, Leon Schiller
arxiv-2502-18346.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Samuel Baguley, Andreas Göbel, Marcus Pappik, Leon Schiller. We study high-dimensional random geometric graphs (RGGs) of edge-density p p with vertices uniformly distributed on the d d -dimensional torus and edges inserted between ‘sufficiently close’ vertices with respect to an L q L_{q} -norm. In this setting, we focus on distinguishing an RGG from an Erdős–Rényi graph if both models have the same marginal edge probability p p .

arxiv-2506-09821.title: Heavy Particle Motion in Rotational Vortices
arxiv-2506-09821.creator: Orr Avni, Alok Kumar, Yuval Dagan
arxiv-2506-09821.description: Abstract This study examines the motion of spherical inertial particles in a three-dimensional rotating cylindrical vortex – a simplified model of geophysical flow structures such as oceanic eddies. The analytical vortex formulation enables the isolation of the key mechanisms that govern particle transport in rotating flows.

arxiv-2602-19092.title: Finite Element Solution of the Two-Dimensional Bates Model for Option Pricing Under Stochastic Volatility and Jumps
arxiv-2602-19092.creator: Neda Bagheri Renani 1, Daniel Ševčovič 2
arxiv-2602-19092.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Neda Bagheri Renani 1, Daniel Ševčovič 2. We propose a fourth–order compact finite–difference (HOC–FD) scheme for the transformed Bates partial integro–differential equation (PIDE). The method employs an implicit–explicit (IMEX) Crank–Nicolson framework for local terms and Simpson quadrature for the jump integral. Benchmarks against second–order finite differences (FD) and quadratic finite elements (FEM, p = 2 p=2 ) confirm near–fourth–order spatial accuracy for HOC–FD, near–second–order for FEM, and second–order temporal convergence for all time integrators.

pmc-10594320.title: Electronic health record–based identification of inpatients receiving antibiotic treatment for community-acquired pneumonia
pmc-10594320.creator: David Yang, Leigh Cressman, Keith Hamilton, Lauren Dutcher
pmc-10594320.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background: Inappropriate antibiotic use for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is common. Although antibiotic stewardship activities require real-time, accurate identification of patients being treated for CAP, there are few reliable methods to identify such patients using the electronic health record (EHR). We conducted a retrospective study to assess the performance of provider-selected antibiotic indication in identifying patients being treated for CAP among a cohort of hospitalized adults.

pmc-11310378.title: Exceptional point enhanced nanoparticle detection in deformed Reuleaux-triangle microcavity
pmc-11310378.creator: Jinhao Fei, Xiaobei Zhang, Qi Zhang, Yong Yang, Zijie Wang, Chuanlu Deng, Yi Huang, Tingyun Wang
pmc-11310378.description: In this paper, we propose a deformed Reuleaux-triangle resonator (RTR) to form exceptional point (EP) which results in the detection sensitivity enhancement of nanoparticle. After introducing single nanoparticle to the deformed RTR at EP, frequency splitting obtains an enhancement of more than 6 times compared with non-deformed RTR.

pmc-11612289.title: Regulatory T cells crosstalk with tumor cells and endothelium through lymphotoxin signaling
pmc-11612289.creator: Wenji Piao, Long Wu, Yanbao Xiong, Gregory C. Zapas, Christina M. Paluskievicz, Robert S. Oakes, Sarah M. Pettit, Margaret L. Sleeth, Keli L. Hippen, Jessica Schmitz, Philipp Ivanyi, Amol C. Shetty, Yang Song, Dejun Kong, Young Lee, Lushen Li, Marina W. Shirkey, Allison Kensiski, Aamna Alvi, Kevin H
pmc-11612289.description: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) with multifaceted functions suppress anti-tumor immunity by signaling surrounding cells. Here we report Tregs use the surface lymphotoxin (LT)α1β2 to preferentially stimulate LT beta receptor (LTβR) nonclassical NFκB signaling on both tumor cells and lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) to accelerate tumor growth and metastasis.

pmc-11679156.title: Botulinum Toxin and Migraine: Goals and Perspectives
pmc-11679156.creator: Maria Pia Prudenzano
pmc-11679156.description: e an effective and well-tolerated therapeutic option, with high patient adherence, several aspects of its use still require in-depth study. Additionally, what is the optimal injection paradigm?

pmc-12467190.title: ErisNet: A Deep Learning Model for Noise Reduction in CT Images
pmc-12467190.creator: Fabio Mattiussi, Francesco Magoga, Andrea Cozzi, Salvatore Ferraro, Gabrio Cadei, Chiara Martini, Svenja Leu, Ebticem Ben Khalifa, Alcide Alessandro Azzena, Marco Pileggi, Ermidio Rezzonico, Stefania Rizzo
pmc-12467190.description: Background: ErisNet, a novel AI model to reduce noise in Computed Tomography images. Methods: We trained ErisNet on 23 post-mortem whole-body CT scans. We assessed the objective performance with mean square error (MSE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index (SSIM) measure, visual information fidelity (VIF), edge preservation index (EPI) and noise variance (NV).

pmc-12750074.creator: Yuechong Cui, Shuting Si, Guannan Bai, Hongxing Jin, Libi Zhang, Xuying Cao, Meiying Gao, Mingyang Zou, Caihong Sun, Amaryllis Mavragani, Claudia Alves, Xiao Hong
pmc-12750074.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). pmc-13048765.title: Bias Patterns in the Application of LLMs for Clinical Decision Support
pmc-13048765.creator: Raphael Poulain, Farzana Islam Adiba, Hamed Fayyaz, Rahmatollah Beheshti
pmc-13048765.description: ObjectivesTo investigate the extent to which Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit social bias based on protected patient attributes and to determine how design choices, such as architecture and prompting strategies, influence these observed biases in clinical decision support.MethodsWe evaluated eight popular LLMs, including general-purpose and clinically trained models, across three standardized question-answering datasets using clinical vignettes.

pmc-13527044.title: GSTM4 Suppresses Prostate Cancer Progression by Targeting TRIM27‐mediated ACLY Ubiquitination and Lipid Metabolism
pmc-13527044.creator: Kang‐Ping Xiong, Fei Liu, Wang Wang, Gang Wang, Kai‐Yu Qian, Sheng Tu, Si‐Ming Chen, Hui‐Min Xu, Shan‐Shan Zhang, Yong Li, Xing‐Huan Wang, Hong Weng
pmc-13527044.description: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a prevalent malignancy in men, and lipid metabolic reprogramming contributes to its progression and therapeutic resistance. However, the drivers of lipid metabolic dysregulation in PCa remain incompletely defined. Through transcriptomic sequencing of PCa patient tissues, we identified glutathione S‐transferase mu 4 (GSTM4) as a novel regulator of lipid metabolism.

pmc-13621296.title: Amiodarone-induced liver injury with bright liver sign: A case report
pmc-13621296.creator: Zheng-Qing Shen, Xiao-Xiao Xia, Die-Wen Dong, Xian-Feng Zhang, Nan-Jing Shi
pmc-13621296.description: BACKGROUNDAmiodarone is an antiarrhythmic drug with well-recognized hepatotoxicity; however, its radiologic appearance mimicking hepatic iron deposition has been rarely reported. We describe a case in which the initial imaging findings were misinterpreted as hemochromatosis, whereas the final diagnosis was amiodarone-induced liver injury (AILI).
